questions.passage:
The table below shows patient outcomes for a new cardiac medication across three dosage groups:

| Dosage Group | Patients | Improved | No Change | Worsened |
|--------------|----------|----------|-----------|----------|
| Low (10 mg)  | 150      | 60       | 65        | 25       |
| Medium (20 mg) | 200    | 100      | 70        | 30       |
| High (40 mg) | 180      | 108      | 45        | 27       |
questions.question: What percentage of patients in the High dosage group improved? (Round to nearest whole number)
questions.explanation: Improved in High group = 108 out of 180. (108/180) × 100 = 60%.

questions.passage: A hospital treated 3,200 patients last year. This year, admissions decreased by 12% for surgical cases and increased by 8% for medical cases. Surgical cases made up 45% of last year's total, and medical cases made up 55%.
questions.question: How many surgical patients were treated this year?
questions.explanation: Last year surgical = 3,200 × 0.45 = 1,440. This year surgical = 1,440 × 0.88 = 1,267.2 ≈ 1,267.

questions.passage: An infusion pump delivers 500 mL of normal saline over 8 hours. The nurse notes the bag started at 08:00.
questions.question: At what rate in mL/hr is the fluid being infused?

questions.passage: A patient weighing 70 kg requires adrenaline at a dose of 0.01 mg/kg. The adrenaline solution is supplied at a concentration of 1 mg/mL (1:1000).
questions.question: How many mL of adrenaline solution should be administered?
questions.explanation: Dose needed = 70 kg × 0.01 mg/kg = 0.7 mg. Concentration = 1 mg/mL. Volume = 0.7 mg ÷ 1 mg/mL = 0.7 mL.

questions.passage:
The table shows the annual budget allocation for a regional hospital (total budget: £8.5 million):

| Department | Allocation |
|------------|------------|
| Emergency  | 25%        |
| Surgery    | 30%        |
| Paediatrics | 15%       |
| Oncology   | 20%        |
| Admin      | 10%        |
questions.question: How much more does Surgery receive compared to Oncology?

questions.passage: A hospital ward has 45 beds allocated in the ratio of medical : surgical : observation = 5 : 3 : 1.
questions.question: How many beds are allocated to surgical patients?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 5 + 3 + 1 = 9. Each part = 45 ÷ 9 = 5. Surgical = 3 × 5 = 15 beds.

questions.question: What was the average wait time on Fridays across all four weeks?

questions.passage: A pharmaceutical company tested a new antibiotic on 500 patients. 380 responded positively. The company claims a 76% success rate. A competitor drug shows a 70% success rate.
questions.question: By how many percentage points does the new drug exceed the competitor's success rate?
questions.explanation: New drug success = 380/500 = 76%. Difference = 76% − 70% = 6 percentage points.

questions.passage: A patient requires morphine at 2 mg/kg. The morphine solution has a concentration of 10 mg/mL. The patient weighs 68 kg.
questions.question: How many mL of morphine solution should be administered? (Round to one decimal place)
questions.explanation: Dose = 68 kg × 2 mg/kg = 136 mg. Volume = 136 mg ÷ 10 mg/mL = 13.6 mL.

questions.passage: An emergency department treats 48 patients between 08:00 and 16:00. The department has 4 treatment bays, each used equally.
questions.question: On average, how many minutes does each treatment bay take per patient?
questions.explanation: Total time = 8 hours = 480 minutes. Patients per bay = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 patients. Minutes per patient per bay = 480 ÷ 12 = 40 minutes.
